home.title: Home
paragraphs: Your professional profile home page after sign-in.
Numbers and charts show how many jobs, courses, studies, and other details you have filled in. A more complete profile produces a better exported CV.
Profile completeness points out important details that are still missing, such as contact information, photo, or professional summary.
Recent activity shows what changed last so you can pick up where you left off.

settings.title: Settings
paragraphs: Your main profile details live here: name, contact information, photo, address, and the professional summary on your CV.
The summary can be written in more than one language, which helps when your CV is read abroad.
In main skills, you choose what to highlight and the order in which skills appear on your CV.
Download generates a PDF with your profile, jobs, studies, courses, projects, and skills, in the order you defined.

skills.title: Skills
paragraphs: Words that describe what you know how to do at work, in your studies, or in your professional life.
You can pick from the existing list or create a new one with the name you prefer.
They appear on your profile and on jobs, courses, studies, and projects, showing where you use each capability.
On your CV, profile skills are grouped by category when you set one.

courses.title: Courses
paragraphs: Short courses, certificates, and training, such as a technical course, safety certification, or professional workshop.
Use this area for short-form learning. Formal school, college, or technical studies belong in Educations.
Record who provided it, the period, a description, and related skills. Everything appears on your CV; relevance sets how prominently each entry shows.

educations.title: Educations
paragraphs: Formal studies: high school, technical programs, college degrees, postgraduate work, and similar levels.
Use this area for your main academic path. Short courses and certificates belong in Courses.
Record the institution, level, status, period, and a description. You can attach skills gained in that study.
On your CV, more relevant educations appear with greater prominence.

organizations.title: Organizations
paragraphs: Companies, schools, and institutions you mention on your CV, whether where you worked, studied, or took a course.
Save each name once and reuse it when recording jobs, studies, or courses. If it is not on the list, create it with the correct name.
The name appears with the records that use it, as a shared reference across your CV.

projects.title: Projects
paragraphs: Work done on your own or alongside a job, such as freelance jobs, renovations, volunteer work, or a deliverable you want to highlight beyond the job title.
Describe what you did, attach skills that work demonstrates, and add photos or links if you want.
Relevance sets how prominently each project appears on your exported CV.

experiences.title: Experiences
paragraphs: Jobs and work in your professional history, each one linked to a company or client.
Within the same experience you can record more than one role, useful when you changed positions without changing employers.
Each role has a title, period, description, and skills used in that function.
Also set the job type and how important that job is on your CV.

apiTokens.title: API Tokens
paragraphs: For when another system needs to read or update your data automatically, without opening the site.
Common in integrations with apps, scripts, or tools that sync your profile.
Each token gets a name so you can recognize it in the list, such as the system or routine that will use it.
When creating one, choose whether it can only read data or also change it. The secret appears once: store it safely and revoke tokens you no longer use.
